proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Confinement-based jamming changes bending response in the tested fiber and granular architectures.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Confinement pressure alters bending stiffness via friction.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P401: confinement-based jamming can change bending stiffness in tested fiber and granular structures.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Direct architecture-scoped findings; wording excludes a universal relation or MP1-R transfer.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Positive-pressure jamming has been demonstrated in tested granular and nylon-fiber structures.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Confinement pressure alters bending stiffness via friction.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P402: positive-pressure jamming demonstrated in granular and nylon-fiber structures.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Direct findings in two pressure-path architectures; no common coefficient or TiNi inference.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Pressure sensitivity can differ between bending/slip branches in the tested nylon-fiber chain.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Confinement pressure alters bending stiffness via friction.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P403: pressure sensitivity can depend on bending/slip branch.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Single-prototype, model-assisted branch interpretation; local slip is not directly measured.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: SMA circumferential tightening changes wire–rubber sliding resistance and structural response in the tested robot.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: SMA thermal actuation can modulate contact friction.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P404: SMA circumferential tightening changes wire–rubber sliding resistance and bending response.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Narrow direct finding is stronger than the broad generalization; no transfer to MP1-R interface is assumed.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Slip-state mechanics provide tested stiffness limits for short steel ropes.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Frictional interfaces create slip-dependent bounds.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P405: equivalent-beam mechanics predicts slip-state stiffness limits for tested short steel ropes.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Validated in the stated steel-rope regime; no hysteresis-cycle law or TiNi transfer.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: NiTi cable/component tests show transformation-sensitive local response in their tension domain.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: NiTi material phase influences structural compliance.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P406: NiTi cable/component tension measurements reveal transformation-sensitive local response.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Direct material evidence, conservatively downgraded for cross-domain pressured bending.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Existing numerical formulations combine transformation-aware response with frictional cable contact.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: NiTi material phase influences structural compliance.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P407: transformation-aware constitutive response and frictional contact can be combined numerically.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Numerical precedent is established; it is not independent physical replication or adequacy proof.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: A conventional continuum friction/slip model exists for vacuum-confined PVC layer beams.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Confinement pressure alters bending stiffness via friction.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P408: conventional continuum friction/slip modeling exists for vacuum-confined PVC layer beams.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Corrected S18 identity and restrictions retained; it is a theoretical/mechanistic analogue, not positive-pressure fiber evidence.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Dedicated specimens can measure selected internal cable-layer or wire–tube sliding resistance.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Distinct internal interfaces can be experimentally isolated.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P409/P413: selected internal-layer and wire–tube resistance tests are methodological precedents.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Methods exist in separate systems; they do not jointly identify MP1-R interface dominance.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: SMA-to-fluid displacement and coupled thermal/fluid/mechanical modeling have prior art.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: SMA as actuator vs TiNi as structural material.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P410: SMA-to-fluid displacement and thermal/fluid/mechanical modeling have prior art.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Direct actuator precedent, but not the proposed spring/piston performance.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Friction/slip constraints can bound or modulate bending response and provide a conventional baseline.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Frictional interfaces create slip-dependent bounds.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P411: slip-state bounds and continuum sliding models provide complementary conventional baselines.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: A called this STRONG, but B correctly separates heterogeneous bounds, models and tests; narrow cross-study wording avoids false replication.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Transformation and contact losses can coexist; global hysteresis does not partition their contributions.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: NiTi material phase influences structural compliance.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P412: transformation and contact losses can coexist; global hysteresis alone does not partition them.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Authors and observations support coexistence, but fractions are not independently measured.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Internal-layer and wire–sleeve resistance methods are distinct identification precedents.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Distinct internal interfaces can be experimentally isolated.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P413: internal cable-layer and wire–tube resistance tests are separate methodological precedents.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Transfer requires matched interface, packing and boundary controls.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Independent pressure and actuator characterization supports attribution of structural versus source dynamics.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Experimental decoupling (Bench A vs Bench B).
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P414: independent pressure and actuator characterization supports attribution.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Method/design rationale, not validation of hardware or evidence that two physical rigs are uniquely required.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Global force–deflection slopes, bending rigidity, DMA loss and loop work are not interchangeable stiffness/loss measures.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Friction, contact and stick-slip; metric caveat implicit.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P415: branch slopes, rigidity, DMA loss and loop work cannot be pooled.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Metric conversion needs geometry, boundary and dimensional checks; S17 is a compatible extension omitted by A.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: Membrane, sleeve and reaction-path mechanics limit transfer of pressure/friction models between architectures.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Pressure-to-friction mapping differs by model assumption.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P416: membrane and reaction-path mechanics can limit transfer.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Supported as cross-study inference; not experimentally quantified in MP1-R.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: The validated corpus does not establish that fluid pressure uniquely determines local wire contact forces or MP1-R bending stiffness.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Outward fluid pressure uniquely increases TiNi inter-wire friction (unresolved).
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P417: fluid pressure uniquely determines local wire contact forces and bending stiffness (unresolved).
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Models assume or infer the map; no proposed-geometry calibration or independent local-N measurement.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: The validated corpus does not establish that global bending uniquely identifies wire–wire versus wire–sleeve dominance.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Which interface actually dominates remains unresolved.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P418: global bending uniquely identifies the dominant interface (unresolved).
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Material, sleeve, contact and end terms are confounded without independent constraints.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: The adequacy of a locked conventional model, and any need for an additional coupling law, remains unestablished.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: A novel constitutive coupling law is required (unresolved).
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P419: conventional model adequacy or new-law necessity (unresolved).
proposition_comparison.adjudication: No MP1-R measurements or locked baseline; failure of one simplification cannot reject the model family.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: It is unestablished whether the SMA spring/piston reproduces the externally imposed structural envelope under matched conditions.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Bench A/B integration losses remain uncertain.
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: P420: spring/piston reproduces external envelope under matched conditions (unresolved).
proposition_comparison.adjudication: No integrated pressure/temperature/loading/history-matched MP1-R evidence.

proposition_comparison.canonical_proposition: The laminar-jamming review provides scoped mechanism orientation but excludes fiber/particle coverage and is not primary mechanics replication.
proposition_comparison.A_GEMINI: Pressure-Controlled Variable Stiffness (review context).
proposition_comparison.B_GPT: S15 use in T01/BP01 as secondary orientation.
proposition_comparison.adjudication: Review scope is retained as context only; it cannot validate positive-pressure fiber/granular mechanics.

hypothesis_comparison.definition: TiNi thermomechanical/material behavior sufficiently explains most observed response.
hypothesis_comparison.missing_observation: Same-lot state/rate/history-matched material baseline plus pressure contrasts with sleeve/end effects bounded.

hypothesis_comparison.definition: Existing contact/friction/stick–slip and transformation-aware material/boundary models suffice without a new constitutive coupling law.
hypothesis_comparison.missing_observation: Locked, calibrated conventional baseline tested on reserved pressure–curvature paths with independent contact/slip constraints.

hypothesis_comparison.definition: Additional coupled pressure–contact–material interaction is needed beyond simpler alternatives.
hypothesis_comparison.missing_observation: Orthogonal pressure/material-state contrasts with local slip/strain and temperature, compared with defined H0a/H0b predictions.

causal_chain_comparison.causal_link: radial reaction → local wire–wire / wire–sleeve contact normal forces
causal_chain_comparison.reason: Uniform confinement or F/μ inversion is not independent local-N calibration; contact distribution and interface sign remain unknown.

causal_chain_comparison.causal_link: local contact normal force → friction capacity
causal_chain_comparison.reason: Coulomb relation and resistance observations provide a conventional route, but μ, N, area, parasitics and history are not jointly identified in MP1-R.
Branches, prescribed limits and sliding regions are model/measurement-specific; they are not local slip fields for MP1-R.
Global response effects are observed in related systems, but material, sleeve, end and boundary contributions remain confounded for MP1-R.
Actuator/source precedents exist, but connected-load pressure-volume and two-location transients are not validated for the proposed spring/piston.

agreement_register.proposition: Confinement effects are architecture-scoped and alter structural bending response in tested systems.
Friction/slip mechanics provide bounds or branches relevant to bending, but do not by themselves identify local forces or a dominant interface.
Interface-specific resistance methods exist in separate internal and wire–sleeve systems.
NiTi state influences response in tested material domains, while transformation/friction loss partition in MP1-R is unresolved.
SMA actuation has prior friction-control and fluid-generation precedents, but the proposed source and structural TiNi roles remain distinct.
No true cross-study contradiction is established after pressure-path, metric, material and interface restrictions are applied.
